# waroom_on_call_team (Resource)

Manages a Waroom on-call team. An on-call team has one or more rotations (e.g. one for weekdays and one for weekends) that decide who is on duty.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# participant_user_subs takes user subs, which can be looked up with GET /api/v0/users.
# Only users who have verified their phone number can join a rotation.
locals {
  alice = "auth0|alice"
  bob   = "auth0|bob"
}

resource "waroom_on_call_team" "example" {
  name  = "SRE"
  color = "1E90FF" # hex format (without #)

  rotations = [
    # Weekdays: hand off every Monday at 10:00, active 09:00-18:00 on Monday to Friday.
    {
      timezone              = "Asia/Tokyo"
      started_at            = "2026-01-05T10:00:00+09:00"
      shift_handoff_time    = "10:00"
      shift_handoff_wday    = 1 # Monday
      participant_user_subs = [local.alice, local.bob]
      time_slots = [
        for day in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] : { day_of_week = day, start_time = "09:00", end_time = "18:00" }
      ]
    },
    # Off hours: hand off every day at 18:00, always active.
    # Rotations earlier in the list take priority where their time slots overlap.
    {
      timezone              = "Asia/Tokyo"
      started_at            = "2026-01-05T18:00:00+09:00"
      shift_handoff_time    = "18:00"
      interval_days         = 1 # shift_handoff_wday must be omitted unless interval_days is a multiple of 7
      participant_user_subs = [local.bob, local.alice]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `color` (String) The color of the on-call team, as a 6-digit hex code without `#` (e.g. `FF0000`).
- `name` (String) The name of the on-call team.
- `rotations` (Attributes List) The rotations of the team. At least one is required. The list order is the priority: when the active times of rotations overlap, the on-duty participant of the earlier rotation is called. Rotations are matched to the existing ones by their position in the list, so removing or reordering rotations updates the existing rotations in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rotations))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) On-call team ID. This is an alias for `uuid`.
- `uuid` (String) The unique identifier (UUID) of the on-call team. This is automatically generated by Waroom.

<a id="nestedatt--rotations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rotations`

Required:

- `shift_handoff_time` (String) The time of day (`HH:MM`) when the shift is handed off to the next participant.
- `started_at` (String) The date and time the first shift starts, in RFC 3339 format (e.g. `2026-01-05T10:00:00+09:00`). Waroom adjusts it to a shift handoff: when `interval_days` is a multiple of 7, to the latest handoff (`shift_handoff_wday` and `shift_handoff_time`) at or before this time; otherwise, to `shift_handoff_time` on the same day. The configured value is kept in the state, and a change is shown only when the start is changed outside Terraform.
- `timezone` (String) The timezone of the rotation, in IANA format (e.g. `Asia/Tokyo`). `shift_handoff_time` and `time_slots` are interpreted in this timezone.

Optional:

- `interval_days` (Number) The number of days between shift handoffs (1-14). Defaults to `7` (weekly).
- `participant_user_subs` (List of String) The `sub` of the users in the rotation, in on-duty order. Only users who have verified their phone number can be added. Defaults to no participants.
- `shift_handoff_wday` (Number) The day of the week the shift is handed off (0 is Sunday, 6 is Saturday). Required when `interval_days` is a multiple of 7, and must be omitted otherwise.
- `time_slots` (Attributes Set) The days of the week and times when the rotation is active. Defaults to none, which means always active. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rotations--time_slots))

Read-Only:

- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the rotation.

<a id="nestedatt--rotations--time_slots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rotations.time_slots`

Required:

- `day_of_week` (Number) The day of the week (0 is Sunday, 6 is Saturday).
- `end_time` (String) The end time (`HH:MM`). A time earlier than `start_time` continues into the next day (e.g. `22:00`-`02:00`), and `23:59` includes the end of the day.
- `start_time` (String) The start time (`HH:MM`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# On-call teams can be imported by specifying the team UUID
import {
  to = waroom_on_call_team.example
  id = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# On-call teams can be imported by specifying the team UUID
terraform import waroom_on_call_team.example 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
```
